Subject: Draft redlines for pilot MSA & Order Form — governing seat + emergency relief

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attaching our first-pass redlines for the MSA and the Order Form for the HarborAI pilot. Two items we flagged as discussion points so legal can triage quickly:

1) Governing law and forum: our standard is Delaware law with courts in Delaware for injunctive relief and enforcement. HarborAI had asked for California. We redlined a middle path that preserves Delaware for contract interpretation but allows expedited provisional relief in CA state/federal court for urgent preservation.

2) Emergency / equitable relief: Redwood needs a carve for injunctive relief and provisional measures (preservation of logs, KV cache, etc.). We proposed a short emergency-relief carve that allows us to seek temporary injunctive relief in any competent court without waiving arbitration.

Attachment stubs: Redwood_MSA_redline_20280914.docx (redline), OrderForm_HarborAI_redline.yml (order form redline).

Can you confirm whether HarborAI can accept provisional-relief carve language or if their compliance team requires all disputes to proceed first to arbitration? If arbitration must be first, we need to scope an explicit exception for preliminary injunctive relief and for preservation notices.

Next steps: if you’re okay, Laura and I can host a 30-min sync with your counsel tomorrow to walk the redlines.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear notes. HarborAI’s GC team prefers California law for customer-facing contracts, and they are generally reluctant to carve out preliminary injunctive relief that bypasses arbitration. That said, they recognize the practical need for short-term preservation in emergencies.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Can Redwood limit the carve to preservation of data and KV caches only (no broad equitable remedies)?
- Provide a 24–48 hour notification window to HarborAI counsel before any emergency court filing unless there is a true imminent risk.

I’ve looped in contracts@harborai.com — our in-house counsel will review the specific redline language. Happy to do a call; tomorrow morning PT works for us.

—Samantha

Subject: Re: Draft redlines — governing seat + emergency relief

Samantha / Ben —

Appreciate the quick response. A few internal notes for HarborAI counsel to consider when reviewing the redlines:

- Scope of carve: we can narrow the carve to preservation of ephemeral inference state (KV caches, request logs, audit trails) — that aligns with the technical risk and addresses the customer’s ask to limit scope.

- Notice period: we can agree to provide written notice to HarborAI counsel with a 24-hour cure window where feasible, but Redwood must retain the right to seek immediate provisional relief when data at risk is time-sensitive (e.g., deletion of logs, ongoing exfiltration).

- Forum sequencing: if HarborAI insists on California as governing law, we can accept CA law while keeping a mutual escalation ladder: (1) technical ops + legal triage, (2) in-house counsel mediation, (3) arbitration for merits, with an express carve allowing either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in any court for preservation. This preserves arbitration for the merits without blocking emergency preservation remedies.

- Arbitration rules: propose AAA or JAMS in the U.S.; if HarborAI wants arbitration only, we should codify expedited interim relief procedures and specify an arbitrator-selection mechanism for tech disputes.

I’ve highlighted proposed language in the attached redline for ease of review.

Laura Bennett

Subject: HarborAI comments — MSA redline (governing law / injunctive relief)

Hello Priya / Ben —

We reviewed Redwood’s suggested carveouts and have the following counterpoints from HarborAI Legal:

1) Governing law / forum: HarborAI will accept Delaware law for the MSA only if supplemental venue language allows the parties to seek provisional relief in California state/federal courts where HarborAI has material operations. HarborAI will not agree to a unilateral Delaware-court exclusive venue for emergency filings.

2) Emergency relief carve: HarborAI will accept a narrow preservation carve (logs, telemetry, KV cache) but requests limiting Redwood’s remedy to preservation orders (no broad injunctive relief that affects HarborAI’s business operations).

3) Notice & escalation: HarborAI keeps the 48-hour notice where possible; HarborAI’s security team must be part of the rapid triage loop (we added security@harborai.com).

4) Arbitration: HarborAI prefers JAMS. They propose that arbitration be the default for disputes but that interim relief is expressly carved out.

We’ve attached our markup: HarborAI_MSA_comments_20280916.pdf (redline). Please let us know a time slot on 9/17 for a 30-min legal sync.

Thanks,
HarborAI Legal

Subject: RE: HarborAI comments — MSA redline (governing law / injunctive relief)

Team —

Thanks for the notes and for surfacing HarborAI’s priorities. Proposed path forward that should get us to agreement quickly: 

1) Accept Delaware governing law for contract interpretation but include express language recognizing the parties’ ability to seek provisional/preservation relief in California courts where necessary. That satisfies our position on predictability while addressing HarborAI’s operations.

2) Narrow the emergency relief carve to preservation measures only (logs, KV cache, audit trails, and order flow snapshots). No broad business-operation injunctions will be allowed without additional process (showing of imminent harm + attempted escalation).

3) Notice & security loop: update the clause so Redwood must send written notice to HarborAI counsel and security@harborai.com and provide a 24-hour window where practical; Redwood can proceed earlier if we reasonably determine that immediate court intervention is required to preserve evidence.

4) Arbitration mechanics: agree to JAMS and document an expedited interim relief appointment procedure (if HarborAI insists on prior arbitration for merits, we still retain the provisional-relief carve).

If HarborAI can accept those four bullets, we’ll issue a revised redline by EOD 9/19 and prepare a short SOW/order form for the pilot.
